chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from al-Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him)

that a man came to him and said to him: 'O son of God's Messenger, what is the proof for the creation (occurrence) of the world?' He replied: 'You did not exist and then you came into existence, and you know that you did not create yourself, nor did one like you create you.'

key_terms.لَمْ تَكُنْ ثُمَّ كُنْتَ: you did not exist and then you came into existence

ai.seo_question: What is the proof that the world is created according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* presents the 'Argument from Self' (Burhan al-Tanzih), a cornerstone of Shia theological epistemology where the created nature of the self serves as immediate proof of a Creator. Imam al-Rida (AS) emphasizes that since the individual did not create themselves and no peer could have, the existence of the world necessitates a unique, uncaused Creator, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid through introspective reasoning.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 11-32 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (s) - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Ma’bad, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abil Hassan Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (s), “

One day a man came to see Al-Ridha (s) and said, “O son of God’s Prophet! What is the proof that the world is created?” The Imam (s) replied, “You did not exist and were created. You know well that you were not the one who created you, and that there is no one else like you who created you.”
